sources.title: This review’s CPU arithmetic/API and original raw-measurement checks
Possible preservation of local detail and explicit truncation risk
sources.details: For two 4×4 RGB images differing only in red-pixel location, a per-patch red-channel mean maps both to 1/16 at patch size 4; patch size 2 maps them respectively to [1/4,0,0,0] and [0,1/4,0,0]. This is an existence example with hand-set projection, not an accuracy claim. Separately, a sequence with 64 visual positions, 16 prompt positions and 4 answer positions has 84 positions; truncating to its first 64 would remove its answer positions. Increasing configured position capacity alone changes no learned-task evidence.

claims.statement: A visual token here is one patch feature position. For a divisible H×W image the patch count is HW/P²; a smaller patch may preserve local detail, while an increased number of positions alone is not proof of learned understanding.
claims.scope: Square, evenly divisible 16×16 and 32×32 examples and this repository’s learned patch entrance. Local-detail retention is stated as a possibility; this section presents no learned small-object or OCR result.

evidence.locator: section 3.1 N=HW/P² and Eq.1; section 3.2; section 4.1 Model Variants; appendix D.2
evidence.supports: Patch count, trainable patch projection and task-dependent scaling; does not turn local synthetic results into a general performance guarantee.
One feature position per patch and trainable input dimensions.

evidence.locator: red-channel patch-mean constructive example in cpu-check.py; possible_local_detail in cpu-results.json
evidence.supports: A possible difference in preservation of small-feature location without claiming improved learned accuracy.

claims.statement: For H=16, P=8/4/2 yields 4/16/64 visual positions, 24/36/84 total positions with 20 text positions, and 576/1296/7056 full-table cells. H=32 yields 16/64/256 visual positions; the last total is 276 and its square is 76176.
claims.scope: Integer counts, square image height=width, no padding/special-token overhead beyond the stated 20 text positions. This is arithmetic, not model timing or training.

evidence.supports: Exact original printed counts at H=16.
H=16 and H=32 bounded variations plus actual patch tensor axes.
General underlying H×W/P² relation.

verification.observed: All six tuples and actual patch tensors matched exactly; original fence exited 0.
verification.details: Independently evaluated integer divisions/squares and checked patchify produces (1, visual, 3P²) for each case; no training was run.

claims.statement: The full attention table has one query row and one key column per sequence position, so its logical full-table count is N². The square count gives a cost clue rather than an exact elapsed time.
claims.scope: One complete self-attention table per head. Causal masking does not make future source positions accessible; the full matrix dimensions and the number of allowed causal entries are distinct. Kernel, head, layer and hardware timings are not estimated.

evidence.locator: section 3.2.1 Eq.1; section 3.2.3 decoder mask; Table 1
evidence.supports: QKᵀ has query/key axes, decoder future entries are masked, and ordinary self-attention has O(n²d) complexity.
The repo forms the whole score table then applies the causal mask.
For N84, weights shape (1,1,84,84), 7056 cells, with 3570 causal-allowed entries.

claims.statement: An 84-position example exceeds a 64-position model limit. Truncating text can remove answer targets, and merely allowing a larger context does not prove the corresponding task has been learned.
claims.scope: The limit of 64 is an explicit hypothetical scenario, not the historical experiment’s actual configured max_length, which is 128. The bounded check uses fresh untrained CPU parameters solely to verify the rejection contract.

evidence.supports: offset+t is rejected when exceeding configured max_length; it does not silently reuse learned positions.
Visual positions enter the common sequence and answer labels are separate supervised positions.
64-position embeddings accepted and 84 rejected at configured max_length64.

evidence.locator: explicit 64 visual + 16 prompt + 4 answer positional construction
evidence.supports: Shows the stated possibility that a prefix truncation can remove answer supervision; no automatic truncation is attributed to this repo.

verification.expected: Configured max_length64 accepts 64 and rejects 84 with a sequence-length ValueError.
verification.observed: 64 succeeded; 84 raised 序列超過 max_length；增加配置或明確截斷，不能默默重用位置.
verification.details: Bounded no_grad check with width8, one layer, one head. Historical 128 maximum is read separately from raw training/config; no existing checkpoint was loaded.

claims.statement: RGB patches of side 4 and 2 contain 48 and 12 scalar inputs; a 48-column patch projection does not directly accept a 12-value patch. Side8 has fewer patch positions than side4 but a larger input projection matrix.
claims.scope: This repo’s Linear(3P²,16) entrance with matching patch configuration and trained corresponding weights. This does not claim that total parameter count is universally monotonic in patch size or forbid weight-adaptation methods in other architectures.

evidence.locator: Linear original source lines 54-89, affine formula, input and weight shape
evidence.supports: Last input dimension must equal in_features; matrix shape is (out_features,in_features).
Patch projection input is 3P² and position tensor length (image_size/P)².
Weight shapes (16,48),(16,192),(16,12); 12-value patch rejected by the 48-column weights.
Historical candidates use corresponding new VisionEncoder configurations and their own updates, not an inference-only toggle.

verification.expected: P4 input48 and weight16×48; P2 input12 and weight16×12; mismatched input fails. P8 projection16×192 is larger, while sequence positions drop16→4.
verification.observed: Expected shapes matched; incompatible projection raised mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (64x12 and 48x16). Encoder parameter counts P4=1344 and P8=3456 differ by2112, consistent with raw total parameters145664 and147776.
verification.details: CPU shape and parameter checks use fresh encoder instances without optimization. Projection includes bias: P4=784 and P8=3088 parameters; position embeddings decrease256→64, explaining the separate accounts.

claims.statement: The existing limited comparison contains only patch sides 4 and 8; both final image-question results are 9/12. It did not demonstrate a fine-patch advantage or evaluate small text.
claims.scope: Read-only verification of the original seed42 synthetic color/shape comparison, revision22a0bb1b870e4df4af76630243ef55b7ca27840c, original CUDA experiment. One 200-step run per patch configuration; no uncertainty estimate or general patch superiority claim, no new GPU or existing-model reevaluation.

evidence.supports: Recomputed raw before-EOS token exact match9/12 for each, split counts36/12/12, color6/6 and shape3/6, no omitted or failed generation rows; questions only color?/shape?.
Held-out offset families; raw-token exact-match denominator; only patch4/8 candidates independently updated and evaluated.
Original target UTF-8 byte mapping used to recompute exact_match from generated_ids before EOS.

verification.expected: Only patch4/8; each 12 questions, 9 exact matches, 200 consecutive steps, 4765 effective training target positions, 72 effective test target positions; no small-text question.
verification.observed: Every sample’s recorded exact_match agreed with raw generated_ids/target encoding. Both results recomputed as9/12=0.75, with shape3/6 and color6/6. Histories sum to4765 and contain steps1..200. Test raw targets sum to72; splits and samples align; original relevant code hashes equal current source bytes.
verification.details: Original result SHA70898240196727e51cae2e06b5dc5b6ee5f7294579bcd941d65c7ded4b4a6b50 preserved complete. EOS is separately recorded and both eos_rate values are1.0; the accuracy criterion is content token equality before EOS. Original Python3.13.3/torch2.14.1+cu126 CUDA run is distinguished from this Python3.13.5/torch2.14.1+cpu read-only verifier.
